??? quote "Dialogue"

    - Knox, of the Gate Watch. Ten years on this gate. I am the big one; Brindle is the one with the slate. If you are going out, come back the same way, so I can count you in.
    - The egg woman asked after you. She says you have an honest face. From her, that is high praise; she says it about almost nobody, and never about me.
    - The old button-seller sewed a horn button on my coat himself. Says he would not trust the city to do it right. Two faces back on the road, because of you.
    - Look at the posts. An owl on every one. The night watch says it is like having company. Dagny says hers has bigger eyes. It does not. Well. A little.
    - Tick read me version four last night. The true one. He read it slowly, the way Brindle lets him read the slate. Then he said he wants to be like you. I did not know what to say. I still do not.
    - What can I do for you?
        - *Choice:* What are you carving?
        - *Choice:* Tell me about Tick.
        - *Choice:* Who comes up the road these days?
        - *Choice:* Nothing. Goodbye.
    - Foxes, hares, goats. Owls. I worked wood on Workshops Row before the Watch, carrying beams for the rooftop bridges. The work dried up. The habit did not.
    - The owls go to Dagny. I tell her she is the bravest of us. She laughs and thinks it is a joke. It is not a joke. Brindle is still looking for the right words. I decided owls would do in the meantime.
    - My boy. Ten years old and he salutes the cat. His mother had a loud laugh; he remembers that, or thinks he does. He grew up between the guards' boots, here.
    - He wants to be an adventurer, like Hatch. I want him to be a joiner. A baker. A fiddler. Anything with a roof. We have this argument at supper. I am losing it. I know I am losing it.
    - He will go out that gate one day. I know it now. I have stopped arguing at supper; it was only making us both tired.
    - If he must go, I want him taught by the right people. Hatch. Shade. You, *Player*. Do not tell him I said so. He will salute me, and I will not be able to bear it.
    - Carters. Peddlers. Hunters. The cider men. The egg woman. A fellow who brings nothing but bad jokes, every month, and I laugh every month. I know them all by face.
    - When one stops coming, I notice first. I am noticing more of that every season. What I fear is the evening a regular face does not come up the road, and Tick is the one who goes looking.
    - Come back the same way, *Player*. I will be counting.
